featureName: BUG-102-002: projected ml.env omits the sidecar's boot-required ASSISTANT_INTENT_COMPILER_* keys
statusRationale: NOT terminal, and deliberately so. Six of the seven SCOPE-01 DoD items are satisfied with first-hand evidence measured in this session (bundle regeneration, ml.env projection, derived guard + adversarial bite, check, lint, python-compute-only-guard, full unit lane -- all exit 0). The seventh requires building the fixed SST and promoting it to the <deploy-target> target, and NO build, promotion, or host interaction was performed. SCN-102-002-A is therefore unverified. Marking this done would repeat the precise inference this bug punished: the pre-existing boot-safety guard was ALSO green while the deploy was broken, because it asserted a hand-maintained list rather than the sidecar's real requirement. A green local lane is a necessary precondition for the deploy landing, not evidence that it does.
discoveredBy: bubbles.devops, promoting the local-operator build of cf005ed4 to the <deploy-target> target
latency: Latent, not new. The seven keys became unconditionally required in ml/app/main.py::_check_required_config when BUG-069-005 landed, so every self-hosted bundle built since then carries the same defect. It blocked the earlier 02697bfd build from deploying as well, not only cf005ed4.
rootCause: services.ml.env_allowlist in config/smackerel.yaml had no ASSISTANT_* coverage, so the ml.env projection filtered out the seven ASSISTANT_INTENT_COMPILER_* keys that ml/app/main.py::_check_required_config requires unconditionally. smackerel-ml called sys.exit(1) about one second after start, smackerel-core never cleared ML readiness, /api/health?strict=true never returned 200, and the knb adapter's ollama-pre-retirement-proof apply gate refused.
resolution: Two changes shipped together. (1) config/smackerel.yaml: added the PREFIX entry "ASSISTANT_INTENT_COMPILER_*" to services.ml.env_allowlist, chosen over the seven literal keys because the sidecar's required set grows in batches (BUG-069-005 added all seven at once) and an exact list is the same drift trap that produced this bug. (2) internal/deploy/bundle_secret_contract_test.go: replaced the hand-maintained `required` slice -- the thing that drifted and let this ship -- with a set DERIVED from the sidecar sources (the `keys = [...]` literal in _check_required_config plus every os.environ["KEY"] subscript read under ml/app/), guarded by parse floors so a broken derivation fails loudly instead of asserting nothing; added TestMLEnv_DerivedComputeKeySet_HasBite_BUG102002 with two adversarial sub-cases.
designNotes: os.environ.get(...) reads are deliberately EXCLUDED from the derivation, and that exclusion is load-bearing rather than incidental: ml/app/keep_bridge.py reads the managed secret KEEP_GOOGLE_APP_PASSWORD via .get, and spec 102 projects it OUT on purpose. A naive all-env-reads scan would demand that secret be projected into the least-trusted tier, turning a boot-safety guard into a security regression.
affectedSurface: internal/deploy/bundle_secret_contract_test.go (derived boot-required key set + adversarial bite test)

concerns: The four non-boot ASSISTANT_INTENT_COMPILER_* tuning keys (_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR, _MAX_CONTEXT_TURNS, _MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES, _RETRY_BUDGET) are now projected into the ML tier as a consequence of choosing a prefix over seven literals. They are non-secret and carry no credential suffix, and TestMLEnv_CredentialSuffixRequiresSanction_Spec102 still refuses a future prefix-covered key that looks like a credential. Recorded as a known consequence of the design decision, not an unnoticed side effect.
